page.title: Event Run of Show for Professional Services Firms
page.description: A practical guide to building, staffing and executing a run of show that keeps professional services webinars and hybrid events on track.
page.h1: Event run of show for professional services firms
page.definition: A run of show is a minute-by-minute production plan that assigns every cue, transition and backup to a named owner so a professional services webinar or hybrid event runs without gaps.
page.quick_answer: Lock the run of show two to three weeks before a webinar and six to eight weeks before a summit. Assign one owner per cue, rehearse on the live platform two to five days out, and send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours.

sections.h2: What goes into a run of show for a professional services webinar?

blocks.p: A run of show lists every segment, speaker, graphic, poll and contingency in sequence with timestamps and owner names.

ul: Opening slate and housekeeping read by the producer
Speaker introductions with pre-loaded lower thirds
Content blocks matched to branded slide templates
Live poll or Q&A windows with moderator cues
Transition music or video buffers between segments
Backup stream switch procedure and contact
Closing call-to-action and replay timeline notice

sections.h2: How far in advance should the run of show be finalized?

blocks.p: Finalize the run of show two to three weeks before a webinar and six to eight weeks before a summit or hybrid conference.

ol: Intake and brief: confirm goals, audience and platform
Draft run of show: map segments to time slots
Speaker brief and rehearsal: walk through cues on the real platform
Review and approval: stakeholder sign-off on flow and assets
Technical check: verify encoder, backup stream and graphics sixty minutes before go-live
Live execution: producer calls cues, moderator manages Q&A
Post-event: deliver edited recording and clips within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: Who owns each part of the run of show on event day?

blocks.p: Staffing scales with complexity: one producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

ul: Show caller: owns the master clock and calls every cue
Speaker manager: coordinates green room, audio checks and slide advances
Moderator: fields audience questions, triggers polls and keeps chat on topic
Platform operator: monitors stream health, records locally and executes backup switch
Graphics operator: fires lower thirds, transitions and video rolls on cue

sections.h2: Which tools help manage the run of show across teams?

blocks.p: Use a shared calendar for the timeline, a collaborative doc for the script, and a project board for task ownership.

head: Purpose
Common tools
rows: Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard

sections.h2: How does a run of show differ for hybrid versus virtual events?

blocks.p: Hybrid adds venue AV coordination, in-room camera cues and a second audio path that must stay in sync with the stream.

ul: Lock venue AV and platform six to eight weeks out before agenda is final
Assign a dedicated in-room camera operator and audio engineer
Build separate cue columns for room and stream in the same run of show
Schedule a joint technical rehearsal with venue crew and remote producer
Plan a backup stream that can ingest both room feed and remote presenters

faq.q: What deliverables should a production partner provide with the run of show?
faq.a: A production partner should deliver the run of show document, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and highlight clips.

faq.q: When should the full rehearsal happen on the live platform?
faq.a: Run one full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event, then a technical check sixty minutes before go-live to verify encoder, backup stream and graphics.

faq.q: How quickly should the replay reach attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours while the event is still fresh, and include the same call-to-action used in the live close.

faq.q: Can a repeat webinar format move faster from brief to live?
faq.a: Yes, a repeat format can compress the timeline because the run of show template, slide deck and speaker flow are already approved.
